learning: Iteration 9 (±0.07 m span, unscaled weights) lost all oval completions while cutting slalom line loss. Iteration 8 (12 mm) lost all oval completions. The 16 mm, ±0.06 m platform is the only confirmed completion geometry, so this race is a reproduction check before any single-variable change.
notes: Restores the iteration 7 platform and controller unchanged, so the race tests whether the 303.8 result reproduces. Weights are kept at the ±0.06 m scale (about 33 times x) that matched iteration 7.
rationale:
The evidence supports restoring the iteration 7 platform. Iteration 7 (16 mm sensors, x = ±0.06 m at y = 0.02 m, 0.6 kg, 0.12 m body, 0.10 m track, 0.03 m wheels, kp 2.2, kd 0.5) is the only design that completed oval runs (14 of 20, score 303.8). Iteration 8 showed 12 mm footprints remove those completions (0 of 20). Iteration 9 showed the ±0.07 m span also removes them (0 of 20, score 98.4) while cutting slalom line loss to 0.10. The span is therefore the wrong place to change without rescaling, and iteration 9 with unscaled weights is not a usable test. The Builder's intent is to restore this platform, so I keep its geometry exactly.

For the controller, I keep the iteration 7 gains and weights unchanged. The weights [2, 1.33, 0.67, 0, -0.67, -1.33, -2] equal about 33.3 times x, which is the scale that matched the ±0.06 m span. A reduced-gain or re-weighted change would be untested, and the oval completions carry about 500 points each, so I do not risk them without evidence. Oval max_error on finishing runs was 0.048, so the robot holds the line when it is not in a sharp bend. Expected result, not measured: about 14 of 20 oval completions, score near 300, and slalom line loss near 0.3. This is an estimate.
